Chapter Three: The Chapter on Supernatural Powers At that time, the Elder Śāriputra, the Elder Maudgalyāyana, the Elder Ānanda, as well as the devas, māras, brahmās, and asuras, śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, and the people of Jambudvīpa, all conceived this thought:

"For what reason and by what cause has the Tathāgata, the Arhat, the Samyaksaṃbuddha, today in the midst of this great assembly directly spoken only the name of the Buddha-remembrance samādhi (buddhānusmṛti-samādhi), without extensively expounding or analyzing it for everyone, and then risen from his seat to enter the quiet chamber?"
At that time, Amoghadarśin thought to himself:
"The devas, Māras, and Brahmās have all assembled; the World-Honored One now lies on his right side. I shall manifest a subtle display of supernatural transformations."
Having displayed these supernatural powers, he praised and proclaimed in various ways the Tathāgata’s great compassionate merits.

Then, according to those characteristics, he concentrated his mind and entered meditative absorption; by the power of this concentration, he transformed this trichiliocosm so that its ground became as level as the palm of a hand, all made of various wondrous and variegated jewels.
Furthermore, eight rows of trees made of the seven treasures were arranged:
golden tāla trees with silver leaves, flowers, and fruits; silver tāla trees with lapis lazuli flowers and fruits; and the adornments of the remaining treasures were likewise so arranged.
In all Buddha-fields, there were various exquisite adornments such as suspended silk streamers, banners, canopies, wonderful pennants, and precious garlands.
Utpala flowers, padma flowers, kumuda flowers, and puṇḍarīka flowers—such blossoms were strewn everywhere.

Then, Āśūnyaprekṣin immediately manifested great supernormal powers just as he had intended, such that all sentient beings throughout the trichiliocosm—devas, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, and non-humans—were all seated upon lotus flowers made of various jewels. These flowers and petals were innumerable, endowed with perfect colors and fragrances, and each being perceived one another sitting upon those precious lotuses.

At that time, Amoghadarśin, with a mind fixed in meditative concentration, entered this samādhi and manifested great supernormal powers, causing the earth of the trichiliocosm to tremble violently; it was like a round copper bowl from the kingdom of Magadha placed upon a flat stone, tilting and unstable, and the trembling of the great earth was just like this.
If there are sentient beings who hear this sound and are awakened by it, they shall all attain happiness.
It is like the land of Akṣobhya in the east, or the world of Sukhāvatī in the west, where the sentient beings therein rejoice and leap for joy.

At that time, Amoghadarśin again, with a mind of pure, tranquil, harmonious, supple, upright, and straight, and profoundly deep concentration, manifested the miracle of non-action according to its characteristics; thus, while great fierce fires rained down, filling the void of the trichiliocosm, not a single sentient being experienced any heat or affliction of body or mind.
When these sentient beings have their bodies touched by this great fire, once they perceive this phenomenon, their happiness is beyond compare.
It is just as when a bhikṣu enters the fire-samādhi, his body and mind leap with joy;
so it is with them as well.

Then, with a mind of meditative concentration, Amoghadarśin manifested the supernatural power of non-action, causing fine powdered sandalwood incense to rain down throughout the trichiliocosm, its fragrant mists pervading the great thousandfold world system.
If there are sentient beings who smell this fragrance, their spirits are awakened, their bodies find relief, and their joy is boundless.

It is like when Śākyamuni Tathāgata, while practicing the bodhisattva path in a past kalpa, received his prediction of enlightenment from Dīpaṃkara Buddha and attained inconceivable, wondrous bliss of non-arising;
in a single thought-moment, incalculable multitudes likewise obtain such spontaneous delight.
At that time, Ānanda was among the great assembly and had this thought:
"The Buddha has entered his quiet chamber; by whose spiritual power has this transformation been manifested?
Is it by another śrāvaka, such as Maudgalyāyana?"
Could it be Maitreya Bodhisattva, Trailokyavikrama Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Bodhisattva, or Amoghadarśin Bodhisattva?
Only those who have cultivated the Mahāyāna are capable of manifesting such signs of supernatural transformation.
At that time, Ānanda asked Maudgalyāyana:
"The World-Honored One has declared you to be the foremost among the śrāvakas in the mastery of supernatural powers and transformations; is it not you who have performed these transformations now?"
Maudgalyāyana replied,
"Venerable Ānanda!
Why do you ask what the causal conditions for such supernormal powers are?"
"Such a transformation was not wrought by me.
Venerable Ānanda!
What I am capable of is this: I can place this great trichiliocosm within my mouth, yet not a single sentient being would perceive it."
Furthermore, Ānanda!
When I travel to the Brahma Heaven, the resonance of my voice is heard throughout the great trichiliocosm.
It is thus, Ānanda!
In the presence of the Buddha, I let out a lion’s roar, saying that I am able to take Mount Sumeru and place it within my mouth for one kalpa, or even for more than one kalpa. Ānanda!
Furthermore, Elder Ānanda, while I dwell in that Ābhāsvara Heaven, my speech and sounds are heard and known throughout this world. Elder Ānanda,
I am able to move the celestial halls and pavilions of the devas and place them in Jambudvīpa without causing them to shake.
He further addressed Ānanda:
“I am able to subdue the ill-natured and venomous Nanda the Dragon King, Upananda the Dragon King, and all such dragon kings; I am also able to crush and humble Māra Pāpīyān.”
Furthermore, Ānanda!
I went to the east, passing beyond three thousand great thousandfold world systems, and returned to abide within the third world system.

There is a great city there called Ratnadvāra (Jewel Gate), containing six trillion households; I caused every household there to see my body, and further enabled these sentient beings to hear the sounds of the teachings on impermanence, suffering, and emptiness.
Furthermore, Ānanda!
I truly possess these various wondrous supernormal powers, yet I have never before manifested them.

Now, as I sit here upon my lotus throne, I see in every direction, in each and every quarter, incalculable and countless Tathāgatas—all named Śākyamuni Bhagavān—lying on their right sides in their respective monasteries.
"Beholding the Buddha-field with such characteristics, it is as if my divine eye were seeing a thousand worlds.
By whose supernatural power is this manifestation?
At that time, Maudgalyāyana spoke in verse:
"Having cultivated the supreme excellence, I have attained the four bases of psychic power;
now my supernormal powers are peerless, except for the Self-Existent One, the Teacher of the World."
Now I abide here within the realm of Jambudvīpa, shaking those buddha-fields in the eastern direction.
Śakra’s palaces and his celestial maidens, perceiving this trembling, are all struck with alarm and awe.
I am able to swallow and then breathe forth all Buddha-fields, great oceans, mountains, rivers, cities, and villages.
As for Nanda the Dragon King and Upananda, such beings as these are by nature extremely venomous and harmful;
yet by my supernatural power, I am able to utterly subdue them all.
Dwelling in the Brahma palace, my voice and speech cause all throughout this world to hear and know.
Able to stand before the Buddha, one might swallow Mount Sumeru for hundreds of thousands of years, even unto vast eons.
In the world of Flaming Heat, whatever sounds there may be, none fail to be heard throughout this land.
I went to the Jewel City, manifesting my body everywhere,
pervading sixty billion households.
In this life, I have never before manifested such a transformation.
Ānanda, you should know that what I now behold is most excellent and extraordinary—
a marvelous spiritual manifestation and supernormal power.
All sit together here upon precious lotus flowers, surveying the Greatly Powerful World-Honored Ones throughout the ten directions.
Since ancient times, I have never before seen such an auspicious omen.
"I have no doubt that this is either the Tathāgata’s spontaneous miraculous transformation or the majestic spiritual power of a bodhisattva.

At that time, when the Elder Mahāmaudgalyāyana uttered this lion's roar of supernatural power, ten thousand sentient beings all attained human form, became free from dust and defilement, and obtained the pure Dharma-eye.
At that time, Ānanda asked Śāriputra:
"The Tathāgata has declared you to be foremost in wisdom; could this supernatural manifestation not be yours?
He replied:
“Ānanda! It was not I who did this.

What I was capable of was to constantly and diligently practice *vipaśyanā* for twenty years, observing with right mindfulness whether walking, standing, sitting, or lying down; my mind remained clear and tranquil, never wavering, as I analyzed and expounded immeasurable dharmas. Through skillful means and diligent seeking, I did not go beyond the *dharmadhātu*, which only a Tathāgata can fully exhaust.”
"Elder Ānanda! Do you know this?
If I were to place my robe upon the great earth, even though Maudgalyāyana possesses sovereign supernormal powers, he could not move it by exhausting all his strength."
“Venerable Ānanda!
You should know now that I have uttered this lion’s roar before the Buddha;
and all the great śrāvakas, those of great supernormal powers, the learners of the three fruits, as well as devas, humans, māras, brahmās, and asura deities—”
If any śramaṇas, brāhmaṇas, or any non-Buddhist heterodox practitioners from throughout Jambudvīpa,
such as the Nirgranthas, who have come to this assembly, are able to know for themselves that there is no self within the body,
I shall now, through my samāpatti, definitively roar the lion’s roar for them, speaking of the Great Man and the inconceivable.
I say this, with the sole exception of the World-Honored One’s all-encompassing knowledge and vision,
Maitreya Bodhisattva who is in his last birth before Buddhahood, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattvas dwelling in the patience of non-arising (anutpattika-dharma-kṣānti),
the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Samudragarbha-samādhi, the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Supratisthitaguṇa-samādhi, and the Bodhisattva-Mahāsattva Sarvabuddhapratyakṣa-samādhi.
O Bodhisattva.
Great Virtuous Śrāvakas, you may now ask me:
"In such a body as this, what is 'self'?"
"Is it visible? Or is it invisible?
He further questioned the heterodox teachers and various non-Buddhists:
"Regarding the self or soul that you conceive as existing within this body, does it belong to the past, or does it exist in the present?
"Venerable Ānanda! [he asked.]
My such characteristics and various supernormal transformations are manifold; they cannot be known nor seen by Śrāvakas or Pratyekabuddhas. What, then, is "I"?
Regarding what is called "self," in what place does it abide so as to hear such a sound?
Elder Ānanda!

I have always diligently cultivated the deeds of a man, and I have also constantly practiced the conduct of knowledge and understanding. Now I possess even greater mastery over my mind; I am able to subdue the mind, and the mind does not subdue me.
“Elder Ānanda!
I see myself and the devas and humans seated upon great lotus flowers.

Furthermore, I see in every direction, in countless, inconceivable, and incalculable realms, the Buddha, the World-Honored One, sitting beneath the tree of enlightenment; there, the Great Powerful Heavenly Son requests him to turn the wheel of Dharma, and I hear such a voice as I follow along with it.”
With my eyes, I see all manner of various silk canopies, banners, and flower garlands in all the worlds, just as I now see this Sahā world-system.
Venerable Ānanda!
I thought to myself:
"Is this a supernatural feat performed by the World-Honored One,
or is it the work of a virtuous śrāvaka?"
“By what roots of goodness did the Bodhisattva plant in the past that he now obtains such a transformation as this fruit of retribution?
At that time, Śāriputra spoke in verse:
“The Tathāgata is inconceivable; Such are the Buddha’s merits.”
If there are assemblies of Sugatas, whose supernormal powers are vast and inconceivable,
as well as the disciples of the Buddhas— the assembly of those in training and those beyond training—
within this buddha-field, my wisdom is the foremost among them.
Except for those bodhisattvas whose faith and resolve are deep and firm. Elder Ānanda!
In the present and in the future, there is none who can perceive any fault [in them].
Except for the World-Honored One, the Tamer of Men, and those who have set out for enlightenment,
I have constantly and diligently practiced the path of vipaśyanā for twenty full years, observing all phenomena.
Seeking with diligent skillful means, I have never found its limit;
the wisdom I possess cannot be measured.
By the power of my wisdom, I now stand before the Buddha.
I am able to roar the lion’s roar, with the sole exception of those of other paths and those who practice the Śrāvaka vehicle seeking my true reality.
When I manifest supernatural powers and soar through the void,
This land is unseen by anyone; it is the place where I roam.
Even the śrāvakas do not behold it, except for the Heroes of the World.
Apart from the Honored One among Two-Legged Beings and the Sons of the Sugata, none can see it.
Those such as these know my dwelling place;
it is not the domain of outsiders or those with various false views.
My mind always turns with sovereign ease, delighting in inconceivable dhyāna-joy.
If there is a Great Being whose karma consists in practicing the profound path of emptiness—
O Elder Ānanda!
Though I manifest these supernormal powers, the entire assembly of śrāvakas will ultimately be unable to understand them.
How marvelous!
On this very day, I behold all the Buddhas of the ten directions; seated upon my flower-throne, I clearly perceive all the buddha-fields.
Therein are arrayed inconceivable jeweled banners and exquisite flowers and perfumes.
Throughout all worlds, transformations are beyond measure.
O Elder! This is what my mind contemplates:
“The majestic and virtuous Sugatas, and their various miraculous transformations—
these are either the deeds of the Bodhisattva Akṣayamati,
or those performed by others. When Śāriputra uttered this lion’s roar, thirteen thousand sentient beings were freed from dust and defilement, attaining the pure Dharma-eye.
At that time, Mahākāśyapa was also present in the assembly, and Ānanda thought to himself:
"Mahākāśyapa is endowed with majestic virtue and possesses mastery over supernatural powers; could it be that he is the one performing this transformation?"
Thereupon Ānanda asked Kāśyapa,
"Is this miraculous wonder yours,
O Mahābhāga? Kāśyapa replied:
"This manifestation of divine power was not wrought by me.
It is through the power of my wisdom that I am able to discern and manifest all things.
Elder Ānanda!..."
I now stand before the World-Honored One and let out a lion’s roar, capable of drawing into my mouth all the waters within this great trichiliocosm—

the waters of rivers, streams, brooks, ravines, springs, ponds, and the countless hundreds of thousands of millions of vast oceans— and causing them all to dry up completely, yet without the aquatic creatures, such as fish and dragons, perceiving it at all, nor suffering any harm.
“Venerable Ānanda! You should know this:

before the Buddha, in the midst of all the assemblies of devas, worldlings, Brahmās, Māras, śramaṇas, and others, I have spoken these fearless words with the roar of a lion. By my power, I am able to blow away Sumeru, the king of mountains; the great Cakravāḍa mountains; the Himavat, the king of snowy mountains; and even all the mountains throughout the trichiliocosm, reducing them all to fine dust, while those who dwell upon these mountains remain entirely unaware.”
Venerable Ānanda!
I am able to attain such power of sovereign supernormal knowledge.
Furthermore, Ānanda!

Furthermore, I am able to blow forth such power that all worlds within the trichiliocosm simultaneously become fierce, blazing fires, like those at the time when the kalpa-ending conflagration is about to end; yet all sentient beings therein remain unaware of it, none suffer the torment of burning or affliction, nor do they conceive the thought that their world-system is being consumed by fire.
“Such are the marks of my supernormal powers,
Elder Ānanda. Abiding here,

with my divine eye I gaze far into the eastern world-systems, across hundreds of thousands of millions of Buddha-fields, seeing them from their initial burning in various places until they finally become one single fire.”
Having seen this, I thought to myself:
"I shall now manifest supernatural transformations.

Thereupon, by the power of samādhi, I remained in this world as it was and, passing beyond hundreds of thousands of millions of lands to the east, blew with a single breath upon those fierce fires, causing them all to be extinguished at once.
Once the fire had been extinguished, he arose from samādhi and again produced a great, fiercely blazing fire.
"Elder Ānanda!
My marks of supernatural power and my perfections (pāramitās) are thus fulfilled."

If there are those among humans or devas who harbor doubts and lack faith, thinking that the World-Honored One is now lying on his right side, you should go and question him when he rises from his concentration; for only the Buddha, the Tathāgata, can know this.
At that time, while in his quiet chamber, the World-Honored One spoke from afar to Ānanda:
“The Venerable Kāśyapa has delivered a lion’s roar; you should receive and uphold it well.
Thereupon, humans, devas, asuras, and others all joined in praising him, saying:
"How marvelous, Elder!
When Mahākāśyapa uttered this lion’s roar, three hundred million sentient beings all attained human form, became free from dust and defilement, and attained the pure Dharma-eye;
likewise, eighty-five hundred thousand nayutas of devas also became free from defilement and attained the pure Dharma-eye.

The Elder Bodhisattva Akṣayamati, Maitreya Bodhisattva, Mañjuśrī Kumārabhūta Bodhisattva, Trailokyavikrama Bodhisattva, and such immeasurable bodhisattvas as these, all donned the firm armor of great vows. Upon hearing the lion’s roar of the Great Kāśyapa, they took flowers sufficient to fill a casket as large as Mount Sumeru and manifested this transformation to make offerings to Kāśyapa and the entire assembly of śrāvakas.
Furthermore, in the air, seven-jeweled canopies were manifested, each shading one of the śrāvakas.
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa, seeing these jeweled canopies, said to Ānanda:
"This assembly is determined in the practice of the Mahāyāna; thus they perform such various miraculous transformations."
“Elder Ānanda!
Seated upon a lotus flower, I see the Buddha, the World-Honored One, in every direction and location, in incalculable, asankhyeya numbers.
Furthermore, I behold various lands adorned and purified by the seven treasures, interspersed with diverse colors, infinitely subtle and wondrous.”
The sentient beings therein welcome one another, all beholding the signs of abundance and joy in that land.
It is like being atop the Trāyastriṃśa Heaven, intoxicated by flower garlands and attached to jeweled necklaces, where the bodies and complexions of the devas are like the radiance of the moon.
In the void of space, there appeared transformed jeweled canopies, each shading a single sentient being, exactly like mine now, without any difference.
In every Buddha-field, immeasurable bodhisattvas descended from the Tuṣita Heaven into their mothers’ wombs.
“Venerable Ānanda!
The marvelous mastery of conduct and the lion’s roar that I have now witnessed are truly beyond the capacity of ordinary beings; such auspicious signs manifest great supernormal powers.”
At that time, the Elder Mahākāśyapa spoke these verses in the midst of the assembly:
"Ānanda! Standing now before the Buddha, [behold] this trichiliocosm."
In this buddha-field, all the great oceans,
large and small rivers, and other such immeasurable collections of water—
I, by means of my supernormal powers, am able to draw them all up.
Placing it within his mouth, he causes them all to wither and dry up,
yet sentient beings suffer no injury, nor is the nature of water disturbed.
All the Mount Sumerus, Black Mountains, and various other mountains of this world-system—
Abiding in my miraculous power, I am able to blow them all away.
By means of my wise intelligence and the transformations of my supernormal powers,
I shall cause this entire Buddha-field to become smoke and flames.
Sentient beings feel no heat or distress, nor do they have any sense of fear.
While I abide in this realm, I see those lands in the eastern direction—
incalculable buddha-fields— all being consumed by fire.
How marvelous!
This inconceivable power causes that fire to be extinguished instantly.
Having witnessed such supernatural feats and this sovereign conduct, [I am filled with wonder].
I cause countless Buddha-fields to be entirely free from any damage.
Seated upon my lotus throne, I behold these various lands;
they are all exquisite and wondrous, peerless and most sublime.
Furthermore, I beheld the Tuṣita Heaven when the Bodhisattva descended from that realm.
Those who do not doubt the Sugatas and whose minds have attained mastery—
whether they be these Śrāvakas or the Bodhisattva Amoghadarśin— [all witnessed this].
"For the sake of the Great Being Maitreya, why is there such an auspicious sign?
At that time, Ānanda thought to himself:

"This Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra is the foremost among those who preach the Dharma; he is present here in this assembly, possessing great divine power and virtue, having definitively resolved all dharmas and reached the other shore."
"Could these supernatural powers not belong to him?
I shall now question him.
He then addressed him, saying:
“Indeed, Pūrṇa! Is such a portentous sign due to a person of great virtue?
He replied:
"No, Elder Ānanda! By means of my supernormal powers,
for the sake of taming and benefiting all sentient beings, I am able to manifest the power to rub this trichiliocosm with the palm of my hand without causing any injury or harm to the beings within."
If there are sentient beings who delight in the power of supernatural faculties (*ṛddhi*), I manifest the overturning of the great trichiliocosm.
Just as a brave and powerful man might pick up a *kāliṅgaka* coin with his finger and toss it up and down without finding it difficult;
so too do I turn and flip this great trichiliocosm with my right hand, yet not a single sentient being experiences any affliction or harm.
"Elder Ānanda!

If this entire water-element of the trichiliocosm were taken by me with a single touch of my finger and placed entirely within my mouth, not a single sentient being would have any perception or awareness of it."
"I have performed this supernatural feat before the Buddha. Elder Ānanda!

During the first watch of the night, with my pure and sublime divine eye, I surveyed all directions throughout this trichiliocosm to see which sentient beings were hindered by doubts regarding the Dharma, so that I might sever them for them."

As he surveyed the various directions with his divine eye, he saw in every place fourfold worlds; those lands were vast and expansive, and countless sentient beings therein were deluded regarding the True Dharma.
“Venerable Ānanda!
This thought occurred to me:
‘Without rising from this seat, I shall go and dispel his doubt.’”
"Then, with a mind that is pure, tranquil, concentrated, harmonious, supple, and upright as in this samādhi, I shall sever the doubts regarding the Dharma of those sentient beings.
When I expound the Dharma within the assembly, each and every sentient being will feel as though I am speaking directly before them."
"Elder Ānanda!

Since the first watch of the night, there have been countless thousands of assemblies from the four directions who have all attained stable abiding in the Noble Dharma; thirty thousand sentient beings have all received the prohibitive precepts, and sixty thousand sentient beings have taken refuge in the Triple Gem."
Rising from samādhi, I manifest such supernatural transformations and miraculous powers that I am able to completely sever the doubts and delusions of sentient beings.
"Elder Ānanda!

I can abide in this world and, with my pure divine eye, see a realm called Vairambhya in the northern direction—passing thirty thousand lands from this buddha-field—where there is a sentient being who harbors doubts regarding the Dharma."
In this world, the Buddha has entered parinirvāṇa; those who are to be transformed and delivered through the Dharma of the śrāvakas, I thought to myself:
"I shall sever their delusions."
“Without going to that place, I shall, while sitting right here, cause sentient beings to become naturally disciplined and compliant from afar.
“Venerable Ānanda!
Just now, with a mind as concentrated as this, I have entered this samādhi, and countless sentient beings have been illumined by the light of the Dharma.”
With such characteristics, my śrāvakas have already fulfilled all the pāramitās.
Should anyone among this assembly happen to fall into the net of doubt and fail to believe and accept this, they may go and ask the Tathāgata himself when he arises.
At that very moment, by the Buddha’s spiritual power, a great voice resounded from the midst of the sky:
“Ānanda! You have now received and upheld this exactly as the teacher Pūrṇa has correctly expounded it, like a lion.”
At that time, all the people, devas, asuras, and others exclaimed in praise:
"How marvelous!
This is truly rare!"
"If such are the characteristics of the supernatural powers of the śrāvakas, how much more so must be the true realm of the Tathāgata!
When the humans and devas had offered this praise, Pūrṇamaitrāyaṇīputra immediately spoke these verses in the midst of the assembly:
"My outflows are already exhausted; I have certainly reached the other shore."
Forever liberated from all birth, he is the refuge of the world.
Having entered among the ranks of the multitude, yet distinct from them by the Buddha’s supernormal power,
his right hand can overturn heaven, earth, mountains, rivers, and all else.
I shall not allow even a single sentient being to suffer injury or harm. Elder!
Such indeed is the power and efficacy of my supernormal faculties.
If there were the waters of the three thousandfold world-system gathered together,
whether seen or unseen within this Buddha-field, I could,
with a single finger, place them all entirely within my mouth.
I did not allow sentient beings to have any conceptual perceptions or cognitions.
During the first watch of the night, I surveyed all directions with my divine eye:
"Which sentient beings harbor doubts regarding the Dharma?"
Abiding in the power of supernormal knowledges, I shall completely sever them all.
I see a sentient being who has fallen into the net of doubt regarding the Dharma;
yet if they possess a heart of pure goodness and yearn with longing for the Dharma, [I shall deliver them].
Without rising from this seat, I shall completely eliminate their delusions and confusions.
To the multitudes of the four quarters, numbering in the billions, I bestow my pure vision;
I am able to cause them to give rise to faith and inspire them to awaken the bodhicitta.
At that time, there were thirty thousand people who received the prohibitive precepts from me;
sixty thousand sentient beings took refuge in the Tathāgata,
their minds attained tranquility, and they dwelt securely within the True Dharma.
During the first watch of the night, I manifested wondrous supernatural powers;
sitting here in a single thought-moment, I surveyed the northeast,
looking across a thousand lands until I reached the world named Subduing Enmity.
There is a certain being there whose mind harbors doubts regarding all phenomena.
While I dwell in this buddha-field, that person remains in doubt about the Dharma;
desiring to lead them to see the correct path, I shall now resolve their confusion.
"O Elder!
My supernormal powers and the strength of my wisdom are indeed such as this;
only the Buddha can have compassion for all the worlds."
The people here do not believe; you should go and ask the World-Honored One.
Now I sit upon a lotus flower, beholding that Buddha’s parinirvāṇa;
in every direction and land, they are cremating the Tathāgata’s body.
Furthermore, seeing the Buddha’s extraordinary majesty, one wonders:
by whose spiritual power is this?
It is also as I have seen: that all Buddhas enter parinirvāṇa.
Vast, far-reaching, exceedingly sublime and elegant, it is inconceivable.
Is this the work of the Buddha,
or of the śrāvakas?
At that time, Ānanda thought to himself:
"This Rāhula is the son of the Buddha; he possesses great majesty and power, and his supernormal faculties are sovereign. He is also present here within this great assembly."
"Is this transformation not [the work] of yourself?
Ānanda then asked Rāhula:
"You have reached the further shore in the training of the precepts; is this supernatural power yours to perform?"
Rāhu replied, "It was not my doing,
Elder Ānanda!"

With such characteristics as these—possessing hundreds of thousands of kinds of majestic virtue and spiritual powers that are sovereign at will—I am a son of the Buddha; yet whether hidden or manifest, I have never given rise to such thoughts, nor have I ever appeared before you, nor revealed myself.
"Elder Ānanda!

Within this trichiliocosm, I am able—by means of the four bases of psychic power—to place ten billion sets of four continents, ten billion suns and moons, ten billion great oceans, ten billion Sumeru mountains, and ten billion large and small wheel-turning mountains, as well as all other such vast mountains, upon the tip of a single hair. I do so without causing any injury or harm to sentient beings; they are not crowded together within the four continents, and there is no obstruction to their coming and going."
“Such is the mastery of my supernormal powers. Elder Ānanda!
I am able, by means of this entire water element of the trichiliocosm:”

The great oceans, rivers, streams, brooks, gullies, ponds, and marshes, he would suck up with a single pore and place within his mouth; yet their stillness and flow, their tributaries and branches, would remain clearly distinct in their original forms, and the sentient beings therein would experience no change in their nature, nor would they perceive whether the waters were overflowing or depleted.
"Elder Ānanda!
While I dwell in this land, entering this samādhi with a concentrated mind, I behold the Tathāgata Durlabha in the northeast.

Here in this land, at the palace of King Śvetaketu, I take a handful of sandalwood powder and offer it to all the Buddhas of that land; its fragrance is so potent that it pervades the ten directions."
The World-Honored One Duṣprasaha manifested a pavilion ten yojanas high, composed of the seven treasures, and there he burned various celestial incenses.
Furthermore, upon the platform he manifested a jeweled canopy; the height of its base was one billion *yojanas*, and its length and breadth were each exactly one hundred thousand *yojanas*.

All sentient beings within that world together conjured a sandalwood pavilion; the height of that pavilion was one hundred thousand *yojanas*, and its length and breadth were each exactly five thousand *yojanas*.
Thus, immeasurable numbers [of beings] within the jeweled terraces were each individually adorned without obstructing one another.
"Elder Ānanda! Such are the auspicious signs;
I am fully endowed with the pāramitās among the śrāvakas."
